title: Introduce kernel compat proxy to isolate CUTLASS + Triton upgrades
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Upgrading CUTLASS and Triton across our fleet has repeatedly caused subtle ABI and symbol-resolution failures that surface only in mixed-version customer workloads. This leads to emergency rollbacks, platform instability during upgrades, and high dev/ops toil.

Goal: Add a lightweight kernel compatibility proxy (KCP) layer that isolates binary/kernel selection logic from the core runtime so we can: (1) map requested kernels to ABI-compatible variants at runtime, (2) perform lazy probing with safe fallbacks, (3) record detailed telemetry for kernel mismatches, and (4) gate rollout behind a feature flag for canary testing. The KCP should be ABI-stable, small-footprint, and reversible (ability to opt-out per-node).

Scope: prototype in the linux-x86 runtime path used by Hosted and Dedicated. Support mapping rules for CUTLASS v2/v3 and Triton v2/triton-next variants initially. Implement a config-driven mapping table, a per-process probe cache, and a metrics surface for mismatch counts and fallback latency. Integrate with existing kernel loader and binary registrar without changing public SDK APIs.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel compat proxy implemented and compiled in release build behind feature flag
End-to-end tests pass across CUDA 11.8, 12.x, and 13.x with Triton variants (triton2/triton3) and CUTLASS v2/v3 mappings
Performance regression (p50 latency) <= 5% on representative workloads compared to baseline without KCP
Fallbacks exercised in synthetic matrix and recorded to metrics (prometheus) with metric names documented
Rollout plan documented with canary gating and automatic rollback criteria
Code review approved and PR merged, QA sign-off on Dedicated staging cluster
design_decisions: Use process-local compatibility proxy (library + small registrar shim) instead of centralized routing to reduce blast radius
Mapping table is external JSON/YAML config so Ops can hot-update without binary redeploy
Probe lazily on first kernel bind; cache result per process to minimize steady-state overhead
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: added CPU overhead during first probe. Mitigation: lazy probe + cache and microbench to ensure overhead <1ms median for common kernels.
Risk: incorrect mapping could degrade correctness. Mitigation: conservative default to fallback to oldest-stable kernel, explicit canary rollout, and e2e test matrix before wide rollout.
Risk: operational complexity in mapping updates. Mitigation: provide a validation tool (kcp-validate) and a dry-run mode that only logs mappings.
Risk: cross-tenant behavior differences. Mitigation: include customer-impact label and limit early rollout to non-critical tenants and internal customers.
Risk: security surface for config hot-reload. Mitigation: restrict config updates to signed artifacts stored in S3 with KMS signing and validate on load.
implementation_steps: Draft design doc and diagram (Confluence) -> link in confluence_links
Implement library shim that intercepts kernel registrar calls and consults mapping table
Add probe cache and prometheus metrics hooks
Write unit tests for mapping logic and probe cache
Add integration tests for mixed CUTLASS/Triton permutations
Run perf benchmarks on staging and iterate config to meet p50 target
Prepare rollout plan and feature-flagging in infra
Canary deploy to 5% of Dedicated fleet, monitor 72h, then expand
